our_argument_summary: WIN-066 verdict 'Std Model Explains' is solid: Earth's hemispheric energy balance is nearly symmetric (Stephens 2012); the +0.34 W/m²/decade NH excess is a recently-detected decadal trend (Loeb 2025), not a static feature; dome geometry — taken seriously via inverse-cube integration over a flat disc with a 5,733 km local sun — actually predicts a 90–270 W/m² hemispheric flux difference, 265–794× the cited value, making the WIN claim self-falsifying when the dome's own geometry is honored. The structure is the standard three-prong attack: (1) standard physics already explains the sign through directly-observable empirical inputs; (2) sign-only predictions cannot single out a specific value; (3) the dome must either own the inverse-cube magnitude derivation (and be wrong by ~250–800×) or disown it (and have no quantitative prediction at all). The c6→c7 patch (EXP-534) hardened Counter (1) by adding a 'directly observable empirical inputs' framing, naming three geometry-neutral inputs (continental coverage, CERES surface albedo, aerosol chemistry), and inserting a CERES consistency-trap (the dome cannot accept CERES TOA flux as its +0.34 source while rejecting CERES-derived surface albedo).

holes_found.description: EXP-534 patch claims continental land-mass distribution (39% NH vs 19% SH) is 'a geographic measurement equally true under any projection centered on the rotational pole, independent of the globe/dome geometric dispute.' This overstates the case. Land coverage percentages are computed by integrating land surface area divided by total surface area; both the numerator and denominator require an area metric. Under spherical surface integration the numbers are 39/19; under the dome's own azimuthal-equidistant projection (the natural rendering of land on a disc), equal-latitude bands have a 1:3 inner:outer area ratio — so the SH 'hemisphere' (outer annulus) has roughly 3× the area of the NH (inner annulus), and the per-area land DENSITY ratio shifts to NH/SH ≈ 39 / (19/3) ≈ 6.16, not 39/19 ≈ 2.05. The percentages-as-geometry-neutral-fact claim is therefore not strictly accurate. A defender CAN attack input #1 — though the dilemma-squeeze in Counter (3) closes the escape (if the defender adopts AE-projection percentages, they have committed to the AE metric and thereby own the inverse-cube magnitude prediction; if they reject AE, they have no flat-disc area metric at all). The patch's anticipated_objections #1 in EXP-534.json reasons through exactly this point and references globe-fingerprints/WIN-066.json, but that reasoning is invisible to a reader of the published prose.
holes_found.recommendation: Optional half-sentence tightening: change '(~39% NH vs ~19% SH continental coverage; a geographic measurement equally true under any projection centered on the rotational pole, independent of the globe/dome geometric dispute)' to '(~39% NH vs ~19% SH by total-land-surface inventory; a defender adopting the dome's azimuthal-equidistant area metric instead reaches NH/SH land-density ≈ 6.2 — still NH-heavy, and now committed to the AE metric that drives Counter 3's inverse-cube falsification).' This preserves Counter (1) and pre-emptively closes the metric-circularity attack by routing it into the Counter (3) dilemma squeeze. Not blocking; the verdict and overall argument hold without it.

kernel_of_truth.description: EXP-534 (data/wins.json WIN-066.detail_verdict_text Counter (1) post-patch) preserves the original three-mechanism appeal — continental land distribution, albedo asymmetry, aerosol-radiation chemistry — and the Loeb 2025 source anchor. That structural move was sound from c5 onward. The patch genuinely improves the text by adding the explicit empirical-anchor framing and the CERES consistency-trap (a new structural argument, per EXP-534.json kernel_of_truth field). The original dome insight that hemispheric energy balance is geometrically asymmetric (NP at center, varying firmament height) is itself trivially true on any non-radially-symmetric geometry, and the dome's intuition that this should produce a measurable hemispheric flux difference is even correct — just with the wrong sign of effect (massive, not small) when the inverse-cube integration is actually performed (data/wins.json WIN-066.detail_evidence: '90–270 W/m²').
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The kernel is structurally correct — a non-radially-symmetric geometry DOES produce a hemispheric flux differential — but the magnitude is the WIN's executioner. The dome predicts asymmetry, observes asymmetry, but the predicted-vs-observed magnitudes differ by 265–794× (data/wins.json WIN-066.detail_evidence inverse-cube integration vs 0.34 W/m²/decade). The CERES consistency-trap in the patched Counter (1) further forecloses a 'just disown CERES' escape: the dome cites the CERES-derived +0.34 figure as confirmation, so disowning CERES-derived measurements consistently is incoherent (data/wins.json WIN-066.detail_verdict_text post-EXP-534 Counter (1)). Counter (3) closes the remaining sign-only escape via the dilemma squeeze: either own the magnitude (wrong by 265–794×) or own only the sign (50/50 = coin flip, content-free).

deeper_analysis: The c6→c7 transition centered on whether EXP-534's patch successfully addressed the carry-forward c5 hole #1 / c6 hole #2 ('your Counter (1) appeals to globe-physics, which begs the question against a dome defender'). The patch reframes Counter (1) around three 'directly observable empirical inputs' — continental coverage, CERES surface albedo, aerosol chemistry — and adds an explicit geometry-neutrality claim plus a CERES consistency-trap. Verdict: the patch mostly closes the hole, with one residual minor weakness (the '39/19% continental coverage' phrasing as 'equally true under any projection' is not strictly correct; under AE projection the per-area densities differ, NH/SH ≈ 6.2 instead of 2.05). The EXP-534 anticipated_objections section reasons through this exact attack but the resolution is not visible in the published prose; a sophisticated defender can mount the metric-circularity charge on input #1 without being preemptively refuted. The mitigation is that Counter (3)'s dilemma squeeze still closes the escape: a defender who switches to AE-projection has committed to the inverse-cube magnitude (90–270 W/m²) and lost the WIN. The verdict 'Std Model Explains' holds with high confidence (0.90). EXP-534 was a deep-attack class patch that introduced one new structural argument (the CERES consistency-trap) and successfully hardened Counter (1) against the carry-forward circularity charge — meeting the deep-attack bar. The remaining holes (V51 capture missing, EXP-337 un-integrated) are out-of-scope for EXP-534 and persist as documented carry-forwards.
